name: Royal Library
summary: Tucked deep within the stone wing of Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library preserves the collective memory, chronicle scrolls, and treatises of the kingdom. Under the watchful eye of Head Librarian Milton Sheaf, its shelves hold crucial records of ancient wars, lost legends, and the realms beyond the sea.

sections.title: A Repository of the Realm
sections.body: While Stormwind Keep bristles with armored guards and courtly intrigue, its Royal Library offers an island of scholarly quiet. Overseen by Milton Sheaf, the hall serves as the premier archive of southern human history, preserving surviving texts from before the First War alongside recent military chronicles and recovered tomes. Alliance scholars, priests, and travelers are free to browse its open treatises, which cover everything from the formation of the original Alliance of Lordaeron to the recent emergence of Thrall's Horde in Kalimdor.

faq.q: Where is the Royal Library located?
faq.answer: It is located inside Stormwind Keep, the royal fortress resting in the eastern sector of Stormwind City. Once through the keep's grand foyer, take the corridors leading into the scholar and archive wings.
Milton Sheaf serves as the head librarian. He manages the archive's records and assists scholars and adventurers seeking missing volumes or specific kingdom treatises.

faq.q: What kinds of books can be read here?
faq.answer: Visitors can read historical works covering the Alliance of Lordaeron, the Guardians of Tirisfal, the aftermath of the Second War, and reports regarding the New Horde, alongside regional histories of Stormwind and Alterac.

aliases: who can read in the library
faq.answer: Adventurers from all races of the Alliance may come to the Royal Library to peruse its extensive collection of scrolls, tomes and texts on a wide range of subjects.

angles.text: For scholars of the arcane, the library offers rare primary sources on Tirisfal's past, ancient dragon hunts, and the legacy of the Last Guardian.
The shelves preserve the foundational treaties and war chronicles that bind the human, dwarven, and elven peoples across generations of conflict.
